report_markdown:
## Bottom line
Slatebird's clearest acquisition mechanisms are branded templates leading to signup and referrals rewarded when another team upgrades. Shared boards offer another plausible distribution path, but guest-to-user conversion is inferred, not observed. Three reviews praise speed; none establishes acquisition effectiveness. [S1][S2][S3][S4]

## Snapshot
| Item | Finding |
|---|---|
| Company | Legal identity not publicly available |
| Category | Online team whiteboard [S1] |
| Website | https://slatebird.example/ [S1] |
| Target user | Product and design teams [S1] |
| Model | Free entry; paid editor subscriptions [S1] |
| Evidence date | All supplied pages observed 2026-11-14 |

## Target user and positioning
“Whiteboards your whole team actually uses” emphasizes participation. The homepage names product and design teams; retrospectives, user story maps and roadmaps make the gallery's use cases concrete. Company size is not publicly available. [S1][S3]

## Onboarding
Two entry paths are documented. A template visitor clicks “Use this template” and reaches free signup. A board guest can comment without an account. Signup details, the first authenticated screen and whether the chosen template survives signup are not publicly available. No activation time can be substantiated. [S1][S3]

## Core workflow
The visible outline is choose a template, work on a board, share its link and receive guest comments. Working on the board is an inferred middle step: editing controls and template application are undocumented in the available material. Link sharing and account-free commenting are explicit. [S1][S3]

## Pricing
Observed **2026-11-14**; prices come from the homepage, not a detailed pricing page. [S1]

| Tier | Published price | Known limit |
|---|---|---|
| Free | Free | Up to 3 boards |
| Team | $9 per editor per month | Other gates not publicly available |

The free cap suggests a potential expansion trigger, but the actual upgrade experience is unknown. Annual terms and price history are not publicly available. [S1]

## Growth loops
- **Observed—referrals:** give another team one free Team month; its upgrade earns the referrer one free month, up to 12 months. The reward targets a commercial event rather than mere registration. [S2]
- **Observed—template acquisition:** the gallery advertises 1,400 community templates. Every template page carries “Made with Slatebird” and a signup button. A complete creator-contribution loop is not documented. [S3]
- **Inferred—collaboration exposure:** shared links likely introduce guests to Slatebird without registration friction. Subsequent signup prompts and conversion are unknown. [S1]
- **Inferred—free-to-paid expansion:** free boards likely encourage initial use, with the cap creating upgrade opportunities. Conversion evidence is unavailable. [S1]

## Integrations
Integrations, API access and marketplace listings are not publicly available in the reviewed evidence. Additional searches found no matching source.

## Releases
| Period checked | Finding |
|---|---|
| Recent public release history | No matching changelog located; cadence not publicly available |

## What it does unusually well
Speed receives three separate positive mentions between 2026-08-30 and 2026-10-02. This is repeated praise within four supplied reviews, not a benchmark. Account-free commenting and task-specific template entry points also reduce identifiable participation and discovery friction. [S1][S3][S4]

## Complaints
One review, dated 2026-08-11, reports clunky mobile use and tablet crashes. Treat this as an investigation lead, not a recurring complaint pattern. [S4]

## Takeaways
Separate creator signup from collaborator participation. Tie referral rewards to meaningful outcomes. Connect templates to specific jobs, then measure the signup-to-useful-board handoff rather than celebrating registrations alone. These are analytical lessons from the documented mechanisms, not proven Slatebird results. [S1][S2][S3]

## Assumptions and gaps
The supplied captures are the evidence base; additional searches returned unrelated products. Independent verification, acquisition metrics, detailed onboarding, product documentation, complete pricing terms, integrations and release history are not publicly available in the reviewed material. The review sample is small and its representativeness unknown.
